rubric:
1. Autoregressive generation predicts one token (or discrete code) at a time, each conditioned on the ones before it, with one step per token and a KV cache that makes decoding incremental. It fits text and other discrete sequences.
2. Diffusion starts from noise and runs a learned reverse process that removes noise over many steps, refining the whole sample at once. It fits continuous high-dimensional signals such as images, video, audio, and actions.
3. Classifier-free guidance trains with the condition dropped on part of the steps and, at sample time, extrapolates between the unconditional and conditional predictions. A scale above 1 follows the condition more strongly, usually with less diversity.
4. Names one way to cut the number of denoising steps accurately, for example a DDIM-style sampler that skips timesteps, flow matching or rectified flow with a nearly straight path, a consistency model, or distilling a many-step sampler into a few-step student.
